items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Sonny Henry worked with uh with uh Hippolyte Charles' band with me

ctx.x: yeah this fellow's tall he's he's in those onion and brass bands did uh you ever work with Sonny Henry?

oh yeah Sonny Henry Sonny Henry worked with uh with uh Hippolyte Charles' band with me oh yeah yeah he used to call me G7 cause every time I'd be and they'd be there and sometimes I'd holler to the G7 and they'd call me G7
why was that? he would play on the wrong chord?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: He had Sonny Henry on the trombone. He had Big R on the violin. And I was playing penna banjo.

ctx.x: he was a first class trumpet player where did you work with him what i worked with him at the new Orleans country club i worked at the lions club he had in other words he had a contract with the the lions club the autocrat club and the New Orleans country club and that time we was getting all them two dollars an hour like the musicians getting one

we was getting it then, when things was good, when things was cheap. We used to play a tea dance at the New Orleans Country Club on Sunday evening for two hours, and we used to play every Saturday night out there for a regular dance for the club. And then we'd get our check at the end of the week. See, they paid off with a check. Now he had Camilla Tile on the piano. He had, what do you call this, a trombone player with, got his leg cut off. Big Gasp. No, no, not Big Gasp. Sonny Henry? Sonny Henry. He had Sonny…

they gave them different names, ragtime, this kind, that kind. But they all played a similar style of music, whether they call themselves a different style of band or not. You say that the ragtime band played different, for instance, than the Dixieland band?
